newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: S.E.Asian buyers await further corn and soy falls.
newsitem.headline: S.E.Asian buyers await further corn and soy falls.

text.p: The sharp decline in U.S. corn and soybean futures this week has not lured Southeast Asian buyers who expect the Chicago market to fall further, regional traders said on Thursday.
"We are in a sorting out period. Lots of people are on the sidelines waiting to see how it ends up," a trader said.

Although the Southeast Asian market was quiet, there was talk circulating of Chinese buyers cancelling earlier soymeal and soybean purchases and then re-entering the market for parcels at lower prices, he said.
"There is nothing solid, mere talk in the market. But the probability for it is high," he added.
Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) corn futures closed higher on Wednesday on a technical recovery tied to signals the market was oversold after falling to two-year lows earlier this week.
CBOT soybean futures ended lower, led by the July contract which fell sharply on continued long liquidation.
Singapore-based traders said no big purchases had been seen in corn or soymeal in the region in the past few days.

In Southeast Asia, U.S. corn for July/August shipment was quoted around $120/$122 a tonne C&F compared with $134/$136 last week. Chinese and Argentine corn was indicated at $120/122, down from $132/134 a week ago.

U.S. soybeans were quoted at $296/$301 C&F, compared with $338/$345 last week, while high protein soymeal was priced at $290/$295 C&F, down from $330/$350 a week ago. Low protein soymeal could be bought at $264/$266.
Traders said regional buyers had now mostly covered their positions and were in no hurry to buy.
"When the market moves higher, it will tend to put people into the market," one trader said.
"They have burnt their fingers by paying higher prices. So most buyers are in no hurry."
Another trader said the crop weather was perfect in the U.S. and not bad in China, Thailand and India.
He said the U.S. corn crop does not pollinate for the next two weeks and traders were waiting to see how it would end up.
The trader added that the sharp fall in the Thai baht on Wednesday, following the currency's flotation, had little impact on the regional corn and soymeal market.
"Thailand is a buyer but not a big player in the commodity markets other than rice and sugar."
